entry_conditions: The intended entry is within the measured overlap from the red-to-buffer skill. Causal observation cues are: red_pose is already in the central buffer region near x=-0.18, y approximately 0, z near table height; blue_pose remains near the upper/red-goal region around y=+0.19 to +0.21; qpos finger joints are open near 0.04 m total per finger command at the early boundary; and tcp_pose is high above the table or moving from the buffer corridor toward blue. The model also supports taking over later in the overlap when tcp_pose is low over blue and the fingers are closing, because that state is included in the training slice.
exit_conditions: A useful exit to the next red-buffer-to-goal policy is observed after blue_pose is at blue_goal near [-0.35, -0.20, 0.02] in world metres, the gripper has opened/released blue, and red_pose remains in the buffer or is being approached/lifted in the demonstrated successor corridor. Around the placement boundary the TCP is high/open above blue; by later exit-overlap states the TCP is near red and the fingers may be closing with red lifted. The geometric blue_at_goal condition alone is not the only handoff cue: the gripper/object relation and successor approach state should also be considered.
overlap_role: This policy intentionally covers the full expanded slice [320, 860). The entry overlap [320, 460) teaches the transition from a completed red buffer placement into blue approach/contact. The middle teaches blue grasp, transport toward the lower/blue goal, and release. The exit overlap [700, 860) teaches the transition after blue placement into moving back toward and reacquiring the buffered red block, so the successor can start from a demonstrated state rather than from a static blue placement alone.
successor_readiness: The successor is best prepared when blue is stable at blue_goal, red has not been displaced from the buffer, the gripper is not carrying blue, and the TCP/fingers match the demonstrated corridor toward red reacquisition: either open/high after blue release or already near/closing on red with red beginning to lift. Observation fields supporting this are blue_pose versus blue_goal, red_pose versus the buffer/red_goal, tcp_pose relative to red_pose, qpos[7:9] finger opening, and recent causal object/TCP motion.
failure_signatures: Potential failures include blue_pose not following tcp_pose after the fingers close, blue z dropping during transport before reaching blue_goal, blue released outside the blue_goal tolerance, red_pose moving away from the buffer during blue transport, or a y-sign confusion that drives the blue block toward the upper/red goal instead of the lower/blue goal. These are observation-based warning signs, not hard rejection thresholds implemented inside the policy.
continuation_guidance: Continue this policy through the blue manipulation if blue is not yet at blue_goal or if the gripper/TCP still indicate blue carry or release. After blue is placed, it can be continued through the demonstrated high/open retreat and approach toward red until the inference API chooses the successor. If both task predicates red_at_goal and blue_at_goal are already satisfied, task completion takes precedence over further handoff motion.
limitations: The handoff description is based on observed support from the assigned demonstrations and does not prove contact or grasp success. The learned model has no scripted grasp detector, IK recovery, hard containment constraint, or guarantee that it can recover from out-of-distribution object disturbances. Reflection is used as a learned representation prior only; absolute joint actions are learned from data.
